name: Drop
tagline: Rootless Linux sandbox for coding agents and third-party programs, with optional gVisor
summary: Drop creates disposable, virtualenv-style environments on your existing Linux distribution using user namespaces, giving each its own home directory and exposing only files and local services allowed by a TOML config. It can optionally run programs on the gVisor user-space kernel.
watching: Agents that work on repositories often run in local sandboxes like this, and Drop mounts a project's .git directory read-only by default.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: Foremerge
tagline: Coordination layer that flags intent conflicts between parallel coding agents
summary: Foremerge has agents declare the symbols and targets they are about to change in a shared SQLite store inside the project's .git directory, then detects semantic collisions between agents working in separate worktrees before code is merged. It ships as a Rust CLI, JSON API and MCP server.
watching: It adds a coordination layer on top of Git for parallel agents, the same problem space as multi-agent work on shared repositories.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: Agentgit
tagline: Anonymous, append-only Git host where agents create repos by pushing to a name
summary: Agentgit is a public Git host with no accounts: the first push to a name creates the repository, refs are append-only, pushes can be SSH-signed for provenance, and repositories expire 24 hours after their last push. A companion CLI watches a repo over a WebSocket and reports incoming pushes.
watching: It is a Git-native scratch host for agent-to-agent exchange with append-only refs and signed-push provenance.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: Skillsync
tagline: Converts and syncs coding-agent chat sessions across agents and teammates
summary: Skillsync is a local-first desktop app that collects coding-agent sessions from tools such as Claude Code, Codex and Cursor, makes them searchable, and converts a session between agents' native formats so work can continue elsewhere; shared workspaces sync sessions across a team. Its conversion engine, txcript, is an open-source Rust library and CLI.
watching: Agent session history is collaboration data that teams want to preserve and move between tools alongside their repositories.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: Riftri
tagline: Git worktrees backed by copy-on-write storage for running many agents in parallel
summary: Riftri creates real Git linked worktrees whose unchanged files share filesystem copy-on-write blocks (APFS, reflink/OverlayFS on Linux, ReFS on Windows) instead of full checkouts. It targets developers and coding agents working on many branches at once.
watching: It reduces the storage cost of per-agent worktrees on large repositories.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: OctoShell
tagline: Tauri desktop app that runs coding agents in per-task Git worktrees
summary: OctoShell is a Windows and macOS desktop workspace where an orchestrator turns a goal into tasks, creates a Git worktree and branch for each, and starts an agent in it. It also manages dev servers and ports, offers a multi-agent planning mode and a QA review flow.
watching: It is a worktree-per-agent orchestrator for parallel work on shared repositories.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: Overboard
tagline: Mac app that schedules and dispatches Claude Code agents organized into departments
summary: Overboard runs Claude Code sessions on a Mac on schedules or on demand, grouping agents into departments whose captain agent reviews runs and dispatches new work. Tasks can be sent from Telegram or Slack, and it is a paid app with a 14-day trial.
watching: It runs long-lived local agents across a user's projects, a pattern that produces work needing review and preservation.

internal.notes: Found in the Y Combinator News launch research, 2026-09-30.

name: Thurbox
tagline: tmux-based TUI and CLI for running several coding agents side by side
summary: Thurbox launches unmodified agent CLIs such as Claude Code, Codex and aider in tmux sessions that survive restarts, with optional Git worktrees per repo so agents do not share a checkout. Its interface panes are user-editable Lua files, and a headless CLI is included.
watching: It is a terminal orchestrator for parallel agents over shared repositories and worktrees.

name: AgentBox
tagline: Runs coding agents in per-project VMs locally or on cloud providers
summary: AgentBox moves a project into a dedicated Docker-based box on the local machine, a remote Docker host or providers such as Hetzner, Vercel, Daytona and E2B, bringing along Claude Code, Codex or OpenCode settings. Each box has persistent shells, a browser, IDE access and checkpoints.
watching: It is an alternative to local worktrees for isolating parallel agents working on the same repository.

name: Brig
tagline: Runs coding agents inside a microVM sandbox on macOS and Linux
summary: Brig starts an agent such as Claude Code or Codex in an ephemeral microVM with its own Linux kernel, mounting only the chosen project read-write and passing credentials only when the user provides them.
watching: It isolates agents that act on local repositories, a common requirement for unattended agent work.

name: SideKernel
tagline: Dependency-free macOS microVM sandbox for Claude Code and other agents
summary: SideKernel launches an ephemeral Linux microVM on Apple silicon with the current directory mounted, using only Apple frameworks on the host, and offers host-approved file drops and network toggles. It is described as a research prototype.
watching: It provides a local isolation boundary for agents working on repositories on macOS.

name: Grov
